Anya: Heads-up — bringing Galena-7B through the onboarding pipeline. FP16 baseline looks fine, but int4 quant run shows a consistent fluency drop on the summarization evals.
Kyle: ok, numbers? what quant backend/config?
Anya: using our int4-groupwise pipeline (quantize.py --mode group --bits 4). eval rouge/bertscore drop ~6 pts relative to fp16 on a 1k sample.
Sanjay: did you convert the tokenizer or reuse the repo vocab?
Anya: reused vendor vocab. Noticed a weird token-id cluster at ~43012..43040 that corresponds to rare ligatures/ZWJ sequences.
Kyle: that could interact with rotary freq wrapping. if token ids exceed rotary table length we see phase aliasing.
Sanjay: can you repro with model in fp16 but remapping those tokens to spare ids? quick test idea.
Anya: tried remap -> small improvement but still ~3pt gap. attaching minimal repro below.
Anya: ```
# quick run
python eval.py --model galena-7b --quant int4 --vocab remap.json --batch 8 --max_len 512
``` 
Kyle: couple of things to try: 1) set rotary_base_scale to 10000 instead of default 1000; 2) enable rotary_norm_fix in runtime; 3) run longctx 4096 to surface kv cache aliasing. patch snippet:
Kyle: ```json
{"runtime_config": {"rotary_base_scale": "10000", "rotary_norm_fix": true}}
```
Sanjay: i ran the rotary_base_scale change locally on a subset — perplexity improved 1.8%, rouge +0.9. still not back to fp16 though.
ci-bot: build/quant-smoke failed: int4-groupwise pipeline returned nonzero for galena-7b on test-matrix node-3. see CI run 2026-03-20T15:12Z
Anya: thanks, link please
ci-bot: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/16321
Kyle: hitting the CI run now. logs show weird GEMM mismatch around the embedding projection after quant pack.
Sanjay: embedding projection mismatch + token-id cluster smells like tokenizer normalization difference at conversion time. maybe some ZWJ sequences got split differently between vendor tokenizer and our normalize pipeline.
Anya: i audited a few samples — vendor tokenizer preserves ZWJ ligatures as single tokens, our normalizer NFC -> NFKC pipeline splits them. so mapping isn't 1:1.
Kyle: that explains the remap partial improvement — two problems: rotary phase aliasing for high ids, and tokenizer canonicalization causing different tokenization distributions during eval vs training.
Sanjay: plan: (A) add a conversion step to canonicalize vendor tokens using our normalizer and produce deterministic remap table, (B) run quantization with rotary_base_scale bump and rotary_norm_fix enabled, (C) run longctx kv aliasing smoke.
Anya: volunteer to own A. will produce remap and share diff. target: small script to canonicalize and prefer lower ids for ZWJ ligatures.
Kyle: i’ll own B and C, will iterate on quant params and run 2x shards of the 1k eval set.
Sanjay: i'll run ablation to confirm whether the remaining gap is quant noise or embedding projection packing. will try hybrid per-channel fp16 for projection layer.
Anya: thanks folks. i'll post remap json in this thread when ready.
Kyle: nice. also add a eval tag "galena-onboard-rotary" to the perf dashboard so we can track rolling changes.
Sanjay: small note — when you post remap, include a tiny test that checks tokenization equivalence for 10 canonical sentences.
Anya: will do. TL;DR: two root causes (rotary phase wrap at high token ids, tokenizer canonicalization mismatch). triage owners assigned.
Kyle: :thumbsup:
Sanjay: :+1:
ci-bot: reminder: please attach CI artifacts as links, not large files in thread.
